A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TimeWalker with the same authors, core framework and dataset. All 22 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v2, including appendices, were readable; visual inspection resolved interleaved table extraction. The substantial reorganization does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original rendering comparisons, component ablations, mesh reconstruction, reenactment and dataset analyses in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds identity-consistency measurements, further ablations, robustness analyses and generative-model experiments.

M1.justification: The core Dynamo, residual embedding, DNA-2DGS, Defer-Warping and losses remain unchanged. Appendix I.1.2 adds limited experimental pipeline extensions: LoRA-tuned Qwen-Image generates supplemental training images, and DouBao post-processes rendered outputs. V1 discussed generative priors only as future work.

E1.justification: TimeWalker-1.0, INSTA and the RenderMe-360/NerSemble animation examples are retained. Coverage expands within the existing head-avatar domain through explicit large-yaw and lighting-control scenarios, generative age/pose extrapolation attempts, and approximately 3,000 synthetic training images for Leonardo DiCaprio (Appendices F and I).

E2.justification: V2 extends the comparison scope to generalizable one-shot avatars by evaluating pretrained and finetuned GAGAvatar (Tables 15–16). It also adds an indirect GPHM score comparison, explicitly acknowledging different experimental settings. The earlier comparator set is retained; INSTA++ is newly positioned as a PAV reimplementation rather than being a newly added baseline.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include GAGAvatar testing on three different identities using each lifestage's first image as the source, pretrained-versus-finetuned comparisons, an ArcFace identity metric, and additional controlled component/training comparisons. The stated original holdout rule also changes from the last 10% capped at 150 frames per appearance to an unqualified last 10%; the retained scores do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds residual-embedding placement/removal ablations, a 20-hashgrid setting, training-cost and retained-basis analyses, single-versus-multiple-lifestage training, yaw robustness, lighting disentanglement, and generative-model failure/augmentation studies. However, the numerical loss-ablation rows from v1 Table 2 disappear, although their qualitative examples and discussion remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates or averages without specifying repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added experiments do not introduce uncertainty reporting; the dataset-distribution statistics retain their existing reporting approach.

E6.justification: The original benchmark values match between v1 Tables 5–7 and v2 Tables 11–13. Substantial new results include Table 16's mean identity scores of 86.8 for TimeWalker versus 83.7/80.7 for pretrained/finetuned GAGAvatar. New Table 4 reports single-/multi-lifestage PSNR of 23.69/27.22, but SSIM of 0.959/0.955. Additional robustness, timing and augmentation findings are reported, while the earlier numerical loss-ablation results are removed.

T1.justification: V2 omits the explicit Gaussian-kernel and covariance-matrix definitions, including the flattened covariance expression, from v1 Section 3.1. The neural combination, warping, rendering and loss equations remain equivalent, with several relocated to the appendix. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstracts, introductions and conclusions retain the same central contributions: lifelong personalized head spaces, Dynamo, DNA-2DGS and TimeWalker-1.0, supporting identity preservation and controllable, realistic animation. The additional experiments and preliminary extensions do not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of shared representations and temporal generalization, plus explicit limitations involving yaw angles beyond 45 degrees, lighting/lifestage entanglement, matting noise and inaccurate FLAME fitting. Appendix I also distinguishes the limited benefits of output refinement from targeted generative augmentation and expands misuse and access discussions. These extend the earlier FLAME-expression and incomplete-lifespan limitations.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies 512×512 evaluation inputs, revises reported training time from 3–4 to 3–5 hours, and documents the augmentation images, age/pose captioning and pretrained tools. It updates the listed project-page address and adds a proposed dataset usage-agreement requirement. The A100 hardware, 5,000-step warm-up, 30,000-step training and principal hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around PAV, one-shot head avatars and large pretrained models. PAV is now acknowledged as a closely related approach supporting multiple appearances, qualifying the earlier broad characterization of existing methods. New discussions of GAGAvatar, GPHM, Flux and Qwen extend the research comparison beyond the original reconstruction and personalized generative methods.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: benchmark comparisons move into the main experiments, while detailed losses, age-progression related work, personalized-space visualizations and limitations move into reorganized appendices. The method exposition is compressed, the appendix is divided into thematic sections A–I, and v1's duplicated bibliography is consolidated.

P2.justification: V2 changes the page template and extensively resizes, relocates and restructures displays. It reformats benchmark and hashgrid tables, splits the existing mesh comparison and geometry-loss visualization into separate figures, expands the capability table, and adds tables and figures for the new analyses. Many retained illustrations are moved rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central personalized-space claim: v1 primarily supported identity preservation through image-quality metrics and illustrations, whereas v2 directly measures identity consistency and tests temporal diversity and residual-embedding design. The viewpoint and lighting studies also establish clearer applicability limits. Missing numerical loss-ablation rows, ambiguity about the test cap, and the indirect GPHM comparison weaken reporting completeness, but the targeted validation and more explicit failure analysis provide a substantial net improvement.
